S21.01.note: The name shown is the language written in the reply's code fence, lower-cased; the app does not pick it.
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Type in the message box: Write a short Python function that adds two numbers, in a code block. Send it.
Wait until the reply finishes.
Look at the small grey text at the top-left of the code block. Compare with Expected: it should show the language name in lower case (for example python). A block with no language shows Plain text.
S21.01.where: Chat > send a message that asks for code > read the bar above the finished code block

S21.02.note: Highlighting is on by default in code blocks and no setting turns it off; the colouring is decided in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CodeCard.tsx and apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/syntaxHighlight.ts.
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Type in the message box: Write a short Python function that adds two numbers, in a code block. Send it.
Wait until the reply finishes; the block is not coloured while it is still streaming.
Look at the keywords, strings and numbers in the code. Compare with Expected: different parts of the code should have different colours.
S21.02.where: Chat > send a message that asks for code > look at the colours in the finished code block

S21.03.note: The button is icon-only. Its accessible name is Copy code, and after a copy it reads Copied, or Could not copy on failure (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useCopyAction.ts).
steps: Sign in, open a chat and ask for a short code sample in a code block. Wait until the reply finishes.
Tap the copy icon in the header bar of the code block.
Paste into the message box (or any text field) and compare the pasted text with the code block.
Compare with Expected: the pasted text should be exactly the code, with no language name or header text, and the icon should briefly show a check mark.
S21.03.where: Chat > send a message that asks for code > tap the copy button in the top-right of the code block (its accessible name is Copy code)

S21.04.note: The download button is icon-only and opens the system share sheet (shareFile in apps/mobile/services/fileCreation.ts), not a direct save. Unknown languages get a .txt file.
steps: Sign in, open a chat and ask for a short Python function in a code block. Wait until the reply finishes.
Tap the download icon in the header bar of the code block.
In the sheet that opens, choose a place to keep the file (for example Files), then open the saved file.
Compare with Expected: the file should have a sensible extension (for example .py for Python) and its content should match the code block.
S21.04.where: Chat > send a message that asks for code > tap the download icon in the code block header (its accessible name is Download plus the file name, for example Download code.py)

S21.09.note: The colour comes from the diff code block (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CodeCard.tsx, DiffCodeLines). Whether the model writes a diff fence is up to the reply. Artifact version changes use a similar colour view under Show changes in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx.
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Type in the message box: Show the change as a unified diff inside a diff code block: rename the variable x to total in this Python snippet, x = 1 then print(x). Send it.
Wait until the reply finishes.
Compare with Expected: added lines should have a green fill and removed lines a red fill, each line on its own row.
S21.09.where: Chat > ask for a change as a diff > look at the added and removed lines in the diff code block

S21.10.needs: none (the AGI Code row may depend on the account mode; not traced)
S21.10.note: The side-menu entry word Settings comes from the shared translation file, and the Settings row labelled AGI Code is in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx. Hunks are shown as text from the model's reply, not reformatted by the app.
steps: Sign in and ask for a diff in a diff code block, as in S21.09. Wait until the reply finishes.
Read the lines: each line should keep its own row, and the hunk header lines (starting with @@) should be readable.
Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap AGI Code.
Turn on Show + and - signs in diffs, go back to the chat and open the same diff. Compare with Expected: + and - signs now show at the start of changed lines, with their colours.
S21.10.where: Chat > ask for a diff > read the diff block; Settings > AGI Code > Show + and - signs in diffs

S21.12.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
S21.12.note: The Run code row is only offered in Cloud mode (appMode === 'cloud'); no local sandbox was found in the mobile app. How to switch to Cloud mode was not traced.
steps: Sign in to a Cloud account whose plan includes cloud code execution, and choose a model that supports code execution.
Tap the button labelled Add to chat next to the message box.
In the sheet titled Add to Chat, turn on the Run code row.
Type: Run this Python code and show the output: print(sum(range(10))). Send it, then wait for the reply.
Compare with Expected: a Run code row should appear in the reply with its output, showing the printed result 45.
S21.12.where: Add to chat (the button labelled Add to chat next to the message box) > Add to Chat sheet > turn on Run code, then send a request that runs code

S21.15.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
S21.15.note: Long output is cut to 12 lines in the row; a full-output control exists with accessible name View full output for Run code.
steps: Run S21.12 first so that a Run code row exists.
Tap the Run code row to open its details.
Look under the heading Output (or Response for non-code tools).
Compare with Expected: the printed text of the program (45 for the example) should appear under Output.
S21.15.where: Chat > Run code reply > tap the Run code row > read the Output heading

S21.16.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
S21.16.note: The Stderr section appears only when the program writes to the error stream.
steps: Run this Python code and wait for the reply: import sys then print('ok') then print('problem', file=sys.stderr).
Tap the Run code row to open its details.
Compare the Output section (ok) with the Stderr section (problem).
Compare with Expected: Stderr should show in its own section, in red, separate from Output.
S21.16.where: Chat > Run code reply > tap the Run code row > look for the red Stderr heading

S21.17.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
S21.17.note: The duration chip shows only when the run reports a duration; otherwise the row shows Script or Result.
steps: Run S21.12 in Cloud mode.
Look at the Run code row in the reply, on the right-hand side.
Compare with Expected: a time such as 450ms or 1.2s should show after the run finishes.
S21.17.where: Chat > Run code reply > the right-hand label on the Run code row (for example 450ms or 1.2s)

S21.18.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
S21.18.note: A sandbox error shows as Code execution failed: <error> from apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/toolCallAccumulator.ts.
steps: Run S21.12 (success) and then a failing program such as: import sys then sys.exit(3).
Read the status word on each Run code row: Done for success, Failed for failure.
Tap the failing row and look for the line Exit code 3.
Compare with Expected: success shows Done and exit code 0 in green; the failure shows Failed and a red exit code line.
S21.18.where: Chat > Run code reply > read the status word on the Run code row, then tap the row and read Exit code

S21.19.needs: a Cloud account; a reply that produces a file
S21.19.note: The link from a code run to a generated file card was not traced end to end; the card is built from generatedFile data in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/InlineArtifactCard.tsx and GeneratedFileCard.tsx. The download icon is icon-only.
steps: Sign in to a Cloud account with a chat that produces a file (for example: Create a CSV file with three rows of sample data).
Look for the file card in the reply, showing the file name.
Tap the file card to open the full screen view.
Tap the download icon at the top (accessible name Download artifact), then check the file that is saved or shared.
Compare with Expected: the file should be listed and openable or downloadable.
S21.19.where: Chat > reply with a generated file card > tap the file card to open it > tap the download icon at the top (accessible name Download artifact)

S21.21.needs: a Cloud account with cloud code execution granted, and a model with code execution
S21.21.note: Partly unfinished: the server side needs AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 and E2B_API_KEY in production, which a tester cannot set; if the run fails, record it. The button is hidden while a run is still going or when cloud execution is not granted.
steps: Run S21.12 in Cloud mode and wait until the row shows Done or Failed.
Under the reply's code block, find the button labelled Run again.
If the approval setting is Ask every time, a dialog titled Run this code again? appears; tap its Run again button.
Compare with Expected: a new run should appear with its own output and status, and the earlier run should stay visible.
S21.21.where: Chat > Run code reply (after the run has finished) > tap Run again under the code
